text:
omar: Quick proposal — I want to change RBAC so the security:siem_export group can access exports in s3://redwood-security-logs/ingest/ to support longer retention for investigation bundles. Also planning to use alias/redwood/siem CMK for decrypt. Any objections?

julia: prefer not granting a broad S3 read to a human group. can we scope to a service principal or use a small export-proxy that issues signed URLs?

omar: yeah I was thinking service principal + short-lived creds. the ask originally came from SOC — they want 90d accessible exports for triage, dev wants 365d cold storage.

julia: tiered retention sounds fine. but two calls out: 1) KMS key usage — who can decrypt? 2) audit trail — we must ensure every export/read is recorded in CloudTrail and forwarded to SIEM.

kevin: +1 on signed URL proxy. if we implement a proxy we can avoid giving the security group direct S3 permissions. proxy can authenticate via workload identity and request-per-export short presigned URL. sample IAM intent: 
```
Principals: security-siem-service (role)
S3: Allow GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::redwood-security-logs/ingest/*
KMS: Allow Decrypt on arn:aws:kms:...:alias/redwood/siem only for role
```

sarah: regulatory note — redwood has EU customers; any exported logs containing PII need either redaction or documented legal basis. GDPR requires minimization; for exports used in triage we should default to pseudonymized fields unless explicitly approved. also retention for audit exports may need 7 year retention for certain customers — file a compliance exception if deviating.

tam: infra note on proxy config: we can add an export-proxy Lambda behind ALB that enforces RBAC, mfa-check for humans, and produces V4 presigned urls valid for 15 minutes. config snippet: 
```yaml
proxy:
  auth: okta-workload-identity
  signed_url_ttl: 900
  kms_key_alias: alias/redwood/siem
  audit_event: emit-cloudtrail-custom = true
```

omar: good. one more thing — incident playbook: when active breach investigation is opened, SOC needs read-only bulk access to longer-term buckets. we should avoid ad-hoc IAM changes. propose: a temporary "incident" role that auto-expire and is granted via ticket workflow with approvals from sec-eng + legal. any automation ideas?

julia: we can integrate with our on-call escalation bot to create the incident role and attach a policy for the duration (e.g., 4 days). also create a CloudTrail filter that alerts if any principal assumes that incident role. keep everything auditable.

kevin: vuln triage note — if an incident is tied to a vuln, we must snapshot relevant logs (immutable) and move to cold vault (separate bucket) with stricter KMS policy. prevent deletion by putting Object Lock or MFA Delete where possible.

audit-bot: export_job_1781234567 started by kevin; job_id=exp-20240222-01; files: 3; dest=s3://redwood-security-logs/ingest/20240222/; status=in_progress

sarah: thanks — please include a redaction step or PII tag check in the export pipeline. if any customer PII is present we need either approval or to route to legal.

omar: plan of action from here: 1) tam to prototype signed-url export-proxy + CloudTrail emit. 2) julia to draft RBAC policy restricting decrypt to service principal and incident-role workflow. 3) sarah to confirm GDPR/retention constraints for EU customers and create compliance exception template if needed. 4) kevin to add Object Lock options for archived export snapshots. i'll open a PR with policy and a runbook for incident-role creation.

kevin: sounds good. tagging @sarah for the compliance piece. :white_check_mark:

julia: will review PR, please include an example policy and the audit alert rule.

omar: thanks all — I'll schedule a quick sync tomorrow 09:30 to go over the design. if anyone has objections post here. :thumbsup:
